answer: To defeat Sybil swarms, nodes anchor identity to a cryptographic attestation chain verified by zero-knowledge proofs. Verifiers track an execution thread bound to non-transferable stake; any attempt to wander across cloned agents triggers an exponential capital exhaustion penalty that escalates as 2^n. Rooted like a durable cedar, this mechanism imposes superlinear attacker costs that render large-scale identity replication unprofitable.
